request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This video explains how withholding tax, which already existed for vendors, now also works for employees in Expense Agent. The presenter first covers what withholding tax is and why it matters, then lists the setup options: posting groups, gross or net calculation, simple or compound calculation, and thresholds. A demo creates a mileage expense of about $2,127 above a $1,000 threshold and submits it. After posting, a withholding tax entry of 20% appears (amount 425.40). The presenter then walks through the withholding posting setup, the employee card and the expense category. A separate finance session is mentioned for use outside expense management.

chapters.title: What withholding tax is and why it matters
Withholding tax for employees: setup concepts
Demo: create and submit a mileage expense
Demo: preview posting and withholding tax entry
Withholding posting setup: timing, base, thresholds
Employee card and expense category setup
Wrap-up and pointer to finance session

features.name: Withholding tax for employees
features.description: Withholding tax posting setup, which already existed for vendors from the previous wave, is extended to employees. New fields were added to make it fit employee-related rules, and it works like other taxes such as VAT.
caveats: Setup depends on local authority rules and differs from country to country
prerequisites: Withholding tax posting setup (existing from vendors in the previous wave)

features.name: Withholding posting groups on employee card and expense category
features.description: The withholding business posting group is assigned to the employee card and the withholding product posting group is assigned to the expense category. This follows the same pattern as general business and product posting groups.
prerequisites: Withholding business posting group on the employee card
Withholding product posting group on the category card

features.name: Multiple withholding taxes per category (tax group)
features.description: A category can use a single withholding product posting group or a withholding tax group. A tax group holds several product posting groups, for example federal, state and local, with a component order that sets the calculation sequence.
caveats: Configuration is up to the customer based on local authority rules
prerequisites: Withholding group code defined for the category when using a tax group

features.name: Gross, net or gross up calculation base
features.description: The calculation base can be gross, net or gross up. Gross takes the tax out of the amount paid, while net means the employee gets the full amount and the tax is paid on top.

features.name: Simple or compound calculation
features.description: When several withholding taxes apply to one record, you can choose simple or compound calculation. With only one tax it is always simple. Documentation explains how both models are calculated.
prerequisites: Multiple product posting groups on one record

features.name: Configurable withholding thresholds
features.description: Thresholds can be set per record or line, per document, per category per period, or total in period. The period can be month, quarter, year or fiscal period, and the category can be chosen. The demo uses a $1,000 threshold per category per month for mileage.
caveats: Which option applies differs by country and authority

features.name: Calculation timing: invoice or payment
features.description: Withholding tax can be calculated when the expense report is posted (invoice) or when the employee is paid (payments). With payments, the tax stays unrealized until payment.

features.name: Automatic withholding tax on expense report posting
features.description: A submitted mileage expense of about $2,127, above the $1,000 threshold, produces a withholding tax entry when the expense report is posted. In the demo the entry shows base 2,127 and amount 425.40, which is 20%, and it appears in preview posting.
prerequisites: Withholding tax setup for the employee and the mileage category
Threshold of 1,000 configured in the demo

features.name: Employee withholding exemption and certificate fields
features.description: On the employee card a dedicated withholding posting group can mark a person as exempt from taxation. Optional certificate number and certificate type fields are available when a country requires them.
caveats: Certificate fields are not mandatory and depend on the country

quotes.text: Now we extended bit holding tax to employees as well.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the core change: vendor withholding tax from the previous wave now covers employees.

quotes.text: So you need to make a setup based on your local authorities rules.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that the setup is not one-size-fits-all and depends on local tax rules.

quotes.text: Why I'm using mileage? because I have in a setup that I need to pay taxations if my mileage payment is above $1,000.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the demo scenario: a $1,000 threshold on mileage triggers the tax.

quotes.text: So I have base 2,127 and I have amount 425.40.
quotes.why_it_matters: Gives the concrete result of the demo: the withholding tax entry base and amount.

quotes.text: So everything above uh 1,000 will be taxable withholding tax in 20%.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes how the threshold and the 20% rate work in the demo setup.

quotes.text: So it will be unrealized until I'm paid.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the behavior when calculation is set to payments instead of invoice.

quotes.text: We have documentation about this functionality. So please go there to understand how system calculates both simple and compound models.
quotes.why_it_matters: Points to documentation for the simple and compound calculation details not covered in the video.

quotes.text: because now looking for employee perspective it can be completely different how we uh in which moment we became liable for taxes.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why the threshold options matter more for employees than for vendors.

quotes.text: It can be used outside expense management but we will have separate session about finance.
quotes.why_it_matters: States that the feature is not limited to Expense Agent and points to a separate finance session.
